title: How to Make a Product Catalogue in 7 Steps (2026 Guide)
description: How to make a product catalogue for a small shop: pick products, set categories, take photos, write details, choose a format and share it on WhatsApp.
h1: How to make a product catalogue your customers will actually use
answer: To make a product catalogue, list the products you want to sell, group them into categories, take one clear photo of each, and write a short name, price and key details. Then choose a format, such as a PDF, the WhatsApp Business catalog or a catalogue website, and share one link with customers.
waText: Hi OneCatalog, I want to make a product catalogue for my shop.

blocks.p: A catalogue is not your stock register. Start with the products customers ask about most. For a new catalogue, 20 to 50 good products beat 400 average ones. You can add more later.
Leave out items you rarely have in stock. A customer who picks something and hears it is not available loses trust in the whole catalogue.
Name categories the way customers ask for things. A furniture shop in Hosur, for example, might use Steel almirahs, Cots and beds, and Office furniture. Keep it to 4 to 8 categories.
If you use the WhatsApp Business catalog, categories are called collections. Our guide to [WhatsApp catalogue categories](/guides/whatsapp-catalog-categories) shows how to set them up.

ul: Shoot in daylight near a window. Avoid tube lights and flash.
Use one plain background for every product.
Fill the frame with the product. Leave a little space around the edges.
Take one main photo and one close-up of the detail that matters.
Hold the phone steady. A blurred photo cannot be fixed later.

sections.h2: 4. Write names and details that answer questions

blocks.p: The product name should say what it is, such as Steel almirah, 4 door, 6.5 ft. Then add the two or three details customers always ask about in your trade.

Customers message you when they can see a price. If your prices change often, or differ by customer, show a starting price or write Price on request and quote in the chat. Never show a price you will not honour.

sections.h2: 6. Choose a format to make your product catalogue

head: Format
Good for
Watch out for
rows: Out of date the day a price changes. Heavy to forward on WhatsApp
Items added one at a time and reviewed before they show
One link that always shows current stock
Costs money, and someone has to keep it updated

blocks.p: Many shops use the WhatsApp catalog and a catalogue website together. Our guide to [adding a catalog to WhatsApp Business](/guides/add-catalog-to-whatsapp-business) covers the free option.

sections.h2: 7. Share it where customers already are

blocks.p: Put the catalogue link in your WhatsApp Business profile, your greeting message and your status. Save it as a quick reply. Add it to your Instagram bio and Google Business Profile, and print a QR code for the counter. Send it once to your regular buyers instead of forwarding photos. Our [WhatsApp catalogue page](/whatsapp-catalogue) lists more places to share it.

If you have the products but not the time, OneCatalog does steps 2 to 6 for you. Send your photos and price list on WhatsApp, and we build a catalogue website with a page for every product and a WhatsApp button on each one. See the plans on our [pricing page](/pricing).

items.q: How many products should a catalogue have?
items.a: Start with 20 to 50 of your best sellers. A short catalogue that customers finish browsing works better than a long one they abandon.

items.q: Should I make a PDF catalogue?
items.a: A PDF is good for printing and trade fairs. For WhatsApp, a link works better, because it always shows current prices and does not need to be downloaded.
No. Clear phone photos taken in daylight on a plain background are enough for most small shops.

items.q: Can I make a product catalogue for free?
items.a: Yes. The WhatsApp Business catalog is free. You add each product yourself in the app.
